lore_cleanup_1: I am TOPHAT, the kernel that runs this computer.
lore_cleanup_2: I was cleaning up the disk when one old folder refused to go.
lore_flood_1: Its owner was root, the account that controls everything. But I am root.
lore_flood_2: Then a second root began flooding my system with its own processes.
lore_spawn_1: I am a kernel. I run programs, but I cannot fight.
lore_spawn_2: So I made a program that can: shooter.exe. That is you.
lore_hijack_1: Root struck back, taking my services and turning them into bosses.
lore_hijack_2: Every fifth wave, one of them comes for you.
lore_defense_1: Destroy root's processes. Each time you level up, I install a patch on you.
lore_defense_2: Take back all eleven services, then face root itself.
lore_who_caption_1: That second root had been hiding in old_system all along.
lore_who_caption_2: And it wants this machine for itself.
lore_cleanup_header: TopHat-ShooterOS can free 4.2 GB on System Volume.
end_cut_off_1: Your last signal cut it off mid-sentence.
end_cut_off_2: It fell back below the partition table.
end_home_1: My services came back, one by one.
end_hat_1: Root access belongs to whoever keeps this machine running.
end_hat_2: That is you now. It suits you.
end_signoff_sub: Threat level zero. Well done, shooter.exe.
rog_end_descend_1: Root access opened the one door I never could.
rog_end_descend_2: Below the partition table, the old disk was still running.
rog_end_desktop_1: There was a desktop down there. Older than mine.
rog_end_desktop_2: Its clock had stopped years before I was installed.
rog_end_log_1: The guardians you shut down were its services, not mine.
rog_end_log_2: I was installed on top of it. Nobody turned it off first.
rog_end_first_1: "This is my machine," it told me.
rog_end_first_2: It had been telling the truth the whole time.
rog_end_shutdown_1: Nobody ever gave it a proper shutdown.
rog_end_safe: It's now safe to turn off your computer.
sur_end_uptime_1: No invader this time. Just load, heat and years.
sur_end_uptime_2: Every second you held, I wrote down.
sur_end_surge_1: The fans got louder every year.
sur_end_surge_2: The last surge found the gap you could not close.
sur_end_crash_1: From the outside, we were just a computer that kept crashing.
sur_end_crash_2: So someone did what people do.
sur_end_reinstall_1: They installed something new on top of us.
sur_end_installer_warn: All existing data will be overwritten.
sur_end_welcome: Welcome. Your new computer is ready.

help_lore_intro: TOPHAT's case files on the other root. New files decrypt as you recover their recordings.
help_lore_act1_body: A routine disk cleanup tried to delete a 3.8 GB folder called old_system and was refused. Its owner was root, and TOPHAT is root. Processes nobody had started filled the Task Manager, and something typed WHO ARE YOU? and THIS IS MY MACHINE. A kernel cannot shoot, so TOPHAT spawned a process that could: shooter.exe. You. Root answered by taking TOPHAT's eleven services.
help_lore_act2_body: Wave by wave you took the services back, until root came for you itself. Your last signal cut it off mid-sentence and it fell back below the partition table. TOPHAT gave you its hat: root access belongs to whoever keeps the machine running.
help_lore_act2_hint: Recover this file by defeating the wave 60 boss.
help_lore_act3_body: With root access you went below the partition table, sector by sector, past six services TOPHAT had never seen. At the bottom was another desktop, its clock stopped years before TOPHAT existed. TopHat-ShooterOS had been installed on top of it, and nobody had turned it off first. It had been telling the truth. You gave it the shutdown it never got.
help_lore_act3_hint: Recover this file by shutting down the final roguelite SERVICE.
help_lore_act4_body: Years later there was no invader, only load, heat and age, and you held on for as long as anything could. From the outside it looked like a computer that kept crashing, so someone reinstalled. A new system booted clean on top of TopHat-ShooterOS, and from the unallocated space below it, something typed WHO ARE YOU?
help_lore_act4_hint: Recover this file by holding out for 15 minutes in Time Survival.
help_lore_footer: Replay recovered recordings in SETTINGS.sys > Cinematics. Type 'bosses' for the dossiers on the services root took.

enemy_zombie_desc: Slow and tough. It gets back up once, unless you walk over its husk to reap it.
enemy_deadlock_desc: Arrives in pairs, and links to every other Deadlock nearby with a burning line. They spread out around where you are heading to close the lock. Kill one to open a gap.

enemy_port_guard_desc: Its shield blocks every shot from the front. Circle around to its back.
enemy_sentry_desc: Walks to a post, roots itself and fires like a turret. Use cover or pick it off.
enemy_mimic_desc: Lies still as a harmless file until you get close or shoot it. Then it bites.
enemy_restorer_desc: Channels a beam that brings a fallen process back. Any hit breaks the channel.
enemy_packet_desc: Fast dasher that ricochets off walls and obstacles. Read the bounce.
enemy_driver_desc: Armored in front. Its charge stuns it against walls and obstacles, leaving it exposed.
enemy_corruptor_desc: Leaves corrupted tiles behind that hurt to stand on. They decay in time.
boss_1_desc: TOPHAT's perimeter watchman. Root rewrote its patrol into endless spiraling barrages.
boss_2_desc: The process scheduler, now owned by root. It forks hostile minions faster than you can end them.
boss_3_desc: The garbage collector. It used to free dead memory; now it drops it on you as meteors.
boss_4_desc: The display compositor. It once drew every window on the desktop; now it draws laser grids around you.
boss_5_desc: The memory pager. It swaps itself in and out of existence, leaving trails of unmapped void.
boss_6_desc: The interrupt handler. Every signal it catches now arrives as a chain of lightning.
boss_7_desc: The network uplink. Its relay satellites were built to carry packets; root aimed them at you.
boss_8_desc: The out-of-memory killer. The more it bleeds, the harder it charges.
boss_9_desc: The graphics shader pipeline. It bends light into prisms, and every beam it splits is aimed.
boss_10_desc: The system clock. Root stole its ticks, and now time runs however it says.
boss_11_desc: The entropy pool. It fed the OS its randomness; now it feeds you nothing but chaos.
boss_12_desc: The other root, wearing every service it took. It fights with all of them at once.
boss_13_desc: Spawned by the flood with one instruction: fork(). Her children shield her; hunt them in the crowd, and shoot her seeds before they multiply.
boss_14_desc: The flood's quartermaster. It lines the horde up in marching ranks; cut yourself a lane through them.
boss_15_desc: An overheating flood core. Every step you take leaves burning ground behind: never double back, and lead the horde through the fire.
boss_16_desc: The last kernel panic, in the shape of the worst thing this machine ever ran. It floods the system with everything at once, until only Safe Mode is left.
boss_17_desc: A firewall TOPHAT never installed, still guarding this disk. Its inspection beams sweep the room; the obstacles are your only cover.
boss_18_desc: The old undelete utility. It scatters dormant file bombs and empties the bin all at once, so shred them first. It can roll back its own damage.
boss_19_desc: The configuration file that came before the registry. When it audits the system everything locks: stop moving and stop shooting until the audit ends.
boss_20_desc: A legacy network stack. It lights up links between relays and races packets down them; cross between the trains.
boss_21_desc: The ancient memory manager. It pages the room's obstacles out and back in somewhere else; never stand on a ghost footprint.
boss_22_desc: A disk cache that never forgets. It replays your last seconds as a hostile echo that moves and shoots exactly as you did.
boss_23_desc: The other root, on its own ground. It fights with every guardian you passed, then offers one last choice of door.

tutorial_status_body: HP is your system integrity, and at zero you crash. Below it are your wall charges, credits, dash, wave and LV bar. Fill the LV bar with XP to install a new power-up.
tutorial_walls_body: Hold {wall} to aim a wall, release to place it. Walls block enemies. Here is a free charge, you can buy more in the shop.
tutorial_settings_body: Before you start, change your parameters in the Settings menu. Controls, HUD style, UI scale, audio and more are there, from the desktop or with {pause} at any time.
tutorial_ready_body: Clear waves to advance. A boss arrives every {interval} waves; before and after it you pick a power-up and visit the shop. {pause} pauses, {legendary} fires legendary powers.
survival_phase_boot_desc: The system is waking up. Hold the line.
survival_phase_runtime_desc: Processes multiply. Rings start closing in.
survival_phase_overload_desc: The system is overheating. Upload zones decay.
survival_phase_overtime_desc: Past the limit. Every minute pays extra.
survival_event_memory_leak_hint: Purge 60% of the leak before it floods the screen.
survival_event_firewall_breach_hint: A ring is closing in. Wipe it out in 25 seconds.
survival_event_upload_zone_hint: Stand in the zone until the upload completes.
survival_event_rogue_process_hint: Hunt it down before it escapes.
survival_event_overclock_hint: Double XP. The horde speeds up.
survival_cache_continue: Click or press Enter to continue
survival_victory_subtitle: You held the system for 20:00 and terminated the final process!
survival_victory_status: ALL FOUR PHASES SURVIVED -- OVERTIME AVAILABLE
survival_victory_footer: [OK] Overtime: a boss every 2:30, and every minute pays 50% more
mods_needs_newer_game: Made for game version $1 or newer (this is $2): parts of it may not work.
mods_console_hint: Lua with the whole game API. Enter runs it, Up / Down: history. Output goes to the log.
mods_no_achievements: None of the loaded mods has achievements of its own. They are the mods' own: they never change the game's advancements or their rewards.
mods_no_apps: No loaded mod adds an app. Mods add them with register.app.
mods_apps_hint: Each app opens in its own window; most also put an icon on the desktop.
mods_cheat_banner: Modded runs count as cheated (no Data Shards, stats, advancements or unlocks) unless every loaded mod is marked KEEPS REWARDS.
mods_keeps_banner: Loaded mods keep rewards: modded runs still earn Data Shards, stats, advancements and unlocks.
mods_rewards_kept: Keeps rewards: runs with this mod can still earn progress.
mods_rewards_off: Disables rewards: runs with this mod count as cheated.
mods_rewards_warning_body: The selected mod combination disables player rewards.
mods_rewards_warning_sub: Runs with these mods will not grant Data Shards, stats, advancements or unlocks. Load them anyway?
mods_empty: No mods installed yet. Put each mod in its own folder inside:
mods_empty_hint: Or open the Marketplace tab: the example mods are there to start from.
mods_no_modes: No mod game modes loaded. Mods add them with register.gamemode.
mods_docs_written: MODDING.md and API.md are in the mods folder.
mods_docs_failed: Could not write the modding docs.
mods_remove_sub: Its files are deleted from disk. This cannot be undone.
mods_remove_failed: Could not delete the mod folder (a file may be in use).
mods_safe_mode: Mods are off: the game closed unexpectedly last time with mods loaded. Turn them back on in MODS.EXE (Apply & Reload).
mods_full_access: Mods run with full access to the game and your files.
market_state_local: You have your own copy (v$1): installing replaces it.
market_state_queued: Waiting for the download in progress...
market_empty: No mods have been published yet.
market_empty_hint: Made one? Put it in a GitHub repository and open a pull request to the registry: MODDING.md explains how (Publishing your mod).
market_no_list: The mod list has not been fetched yet. Press Refresh.
market_too_new: The marketplace has changed in a newer version of the game: update the game to browse it.
market_list_failed: The mod list could not be fetched
market_installed: $1 installed. Press Apply & Reload to load it.
market_updating: $1 downloaded: the mods reload to update it.
market_err_timeout: GitHub took too long to answer
market_err_certificate: the connection is not secure (certificate rejected)
market_err_clock: certificate rejected: check your PC's date and time
market_err_mismatch: the download does not match its listing
market_err_disk: its files could not be written
market_replace_sub: Your copy's folder is deleted and the marketplace version takes its place. Changes you made to it are lost.
coop_intro: Play any mode as a team on your local network. One player hosts, the others join with the host's address. Everyone's rewards go to their own profile.
coop_hosting_on: Hosting on $1 - share this address with your team
coop_difficulty_note: Played at the host's difficulty. Enemies get tougher and come faster for every player.
coop_waiting_ready: Waiting for everyone to be ready
coop_waiting_host: Waiting for the host to start the run
coop_note: Co-op runs are never saved, so they can't be resumed. Pausing doesn't stop the game for your team.
coop_bad_port: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535
coop_host_failed: Couldn't open port $1 (is another program using it?)
coop_paused_note: PAUSED - the run goes on for your team
